---
title: "Heading auto-id"
# bd-heading-id-drops-inline-content-fl84n3ql: when a heading carries no
# explicit {#id}, the id is derived from the heading text. The collector
# used to handle only Str/Space/Emph/Strong/Code and discard every other
# inline kind *without recursing into it*, so whole words vanished from
# the anchor — `## Using a "raw" volume` became `using-a-volume`.
#
# Also covered here, decided with the same fix: Pandoc's empty-id
# fallback. A heading that collects to nothing gets `section` (then
# `section-1`, ...) instead of no id attribute at all, which left the
# heading unlinkable and handed `-1`/`-2` to its siblings.
#
# Every id below was measured against pandoc 3.9.0.2, which is the same
# algorithm Quarto 1 uses. Table:
# claude-notes/plans/heading-id-drops-inline-content-investigation/observed-2026-08-13.md
#
# This drives the real render path; the unit-level coverage lives in
# crates/pampa/tests/integration/test_heading_auto_id.rs.
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      noErrors: true
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        - [
            "<section id=\"using-a-raw-volume\"",
            "<section id=\"see-the-docs-now\"",
            "<section id=\"use-strike-here\"",
            "<section id=\"math-xy-inline\"",
            "<section id=\"small-caps-here\"",
            "<section id=\"use-emphasis-and-strong-and-code-here\"",
            "<section id=\"section\"",
            "<section id=\"section-1\"",
          ]
        # The pre-fix ids, and the pre-fix dedup damage.
        - [
            "<section id=\"using-a-volume\"",
            "<section id=\"see-now\"",
            "<section id=\"use-here\"",
            "<section id=\"math-inline\"",
            "<section id=\"small-here\"",
            "<section id=\"-1\"",
            "<section class=\"section level2\">",
          ]
---
